paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see in this chapter. The people were in the twenty-fifth year of their exile, fourteen years after Jerusalem had been struck down (Ezekiel 40:1). Then the LORD takes Ezekiel in visions of God and sets him down in front of a temple, every inch of it laid out. The God who sees what's forgotten had not forgotten His people, and He was already showing them a place to come back to.

Now look at HOW He shows it. The man with the measuring rod tells Ezekiel, "look with your eyes, hear with your ears, and pay attention to everything I am going to show you, for that is why you have been brought here" (Ezekiel 40:4). Gate after gate, the same measurements, and nothing is sloppy or rushed. I think that's the point, baker. When God prepares something, it's ordered, it's careful, and it's for something. Even the rooms for the offerings and the chambers for the priests have a place and a purpose (Ezekiel 40:38, 45-46).

So what do you do with a chapter full of numbers? You pay attention, same as Ezekiel was told to. He was told to report to the house of Israel everything he saw (Ezekiel 40:4), so what he learned wasn't just for him. Same goes for you: slow down in the Word, take in what God shows, and then pass it on. And this tour isn't over, friend. We're only at the temple's front steps.
